notes: All 17 matching source playbooks were read. e5VTP7535II contains no extracted tactical steps or rules, so it contributes no tactical support; its only stated recommendation is two Clan Castle Dragon Riders, one Revive Spell and one Overgrowth Spell.

The most repeated complete troop roster is shared by L1Nk6QhfxmQ and a6fRLOU-bLc. The default spells, reinforcements and loadouts follow that pair. 45MwOV3C1nQ partially matches it but contains unresolved troop entries and a different Grand Warden pet; it is not counted as another identical complete roster.

The matching pair lists three Log Launchers and two Sky Wagons as inventory options. These are not simultaneous battle deployments. Log Launchers are omitted from the troop roster, and Sky Wagon is normalized to the single deployed machine explicitly described by C0lnvxJraoM and u9owFe-ervU.

Support counts distinct videos describing the consolidated action and role. Exact counts, cadences and alternative charge partners have narrower support where specified. Sources with incomplete rosters are not treated as identical army compositions.

Attack time zero represents the stated three-minute deployment. The first Invisibility delay of four seconds translates the stated initial 56-second timer reading. The normal ten-second interval is supported by explicit statements or the 56, 46, 36 sequence. Every six means a countdown reading ending in six, not a six-second interval. b46w2PUASJI also contains a conflicting six-second statement; its explicit ten-second statement and examples are used.

The ten-second cycle assumes Spirit Fox is available with the stated compatible timing. C0lnvxJraoM and b46w2PUASJI prescribe four-second casts if Spirit Fox dies; C0lnvxJraoM also prescribes them near the Clan Castle, Inferno Artillery, Monolith or Long Shot Guardian. The vocabulary cannot detect Spirit Fox death, pet level or all those proximity conditions, so no automatic cadence switch is invented.

All unstated sequential delays are zero. This includes grouped main-army deployments, delayed Royal Champion redeployment, and hero ability setup. Zero preserves narration order without claiming a measured interval.

The default starts the main army before completing the opposite Queen funnel, following the practical sequence in 40ln9NIrCUU, Ff0NfWFgSiY, b46w2PUASJI, eQAelt6VLeE and one u9owFe-ervU example. Other sources establish that flank first. The two-hero and Backpack variants move it before the main entry.

Relative edge anchors translate locations described as this side, a corner or the opposite flank. They do not recover exact tiles. unit_ahead:Royal Champion approximates covering the moving Champion and Spirit Fox. threat:main approximates the narrated dangerous defensive compartment and cannot guarantee a particular backend compartment or coverage of several named defenses.

group_inside:main is the closest available trigger for entry or core arrival. heavy_fire:Royal Champion approximates an unstated low-health or dangerous-charge condition without inventing a health fraction. The early Recall variant cannot verify that the desired funnel is complete. defenders_near:main also includes Clan Castle troops, whereas the Headhunter instructions specifically target enemy heroes.

The default loadout has Rocket Backpack and Fire Heart. No ability timing is invented for its delayed Dragon Duke deployment. The pre-push Backpack variant supplies a sourced activation sequence. Stun Blaster with Fire Heart is a more frequent Duke equipment pairing across the broader sources, but does not match the most repeated complete roster.

The two-hero variant requires its source army rather than the default inventory: L_LKqcL56NE has five Root Riders, eight Valkyries, five Healers, two Ice Golems, one Furnace and supporting troops; six Invisibility Spells, Recall, Rage and Freeze; Siege Barracks, two donated Totems and Poison. Its Duke uses Stun Blaster and Fire Heart. --MRQU7FUxQ instead has six Root Riders, eight Valkyries, one Ice Golem and Barbarian King. Both recall and redeploy the two heroes together; the single redeploy action represents the recalled group.

The Flame Blower opening requires QCrKyyMDYr4's loadout and inventory: Flame Blower and Rocket Backpack on Dragon Duke, four Earthquakes, two Freezes, Overgrowth, Revive and Poison, plus donated Angry Spell and two Totems. The source does not give Earthquake counts per placement; the listed step represents one cast and does not invent the remaining allocation. Its instruction to wait for the Queen to commit has no matching trigger or stated duration; the existing zero-delay sequence cannot enforce that wait.

The Ice Block and revival variant requires rBhknrms4J4's composition: four Root Riders, four Valkyries, five Healers, one main-army Ice Golem and supporting troops; five Ice Blocks, Revive, Freeze, Overgrowth and Poison; Sky Wagon with Inferno Dragons and three donated Totems. Dragon Duke uses Revenge Deck and Fire Heart, Queen uses Magic Mirror and Action Figure, and Royal Champion uses Diggy. Duke-inside and main-group-inside approximate assessing his cleared section and waiting for friendly tanking. The source's instruction to wait for defending Ice Golems to die before deploying Queen cannot be expressed by the available triggers.

The executor's unit: anchor resolves living units. Consequently the revival variant's unit:Dragon Duke anchor cannot locate a dead Duke even though the dead trigger is valid. The sourced revival is retained, but cannot execute faithfully with this anchor vocabulary; no death location or substitute coordinate is invented.

Thrower compositions differ: 40ln9NIrCUU has four Root Riders, seven Throwers, five Healers and two Ice Golems, with Stun Blaster Dragon Duke; b46w2PUASJI has six Root Riders, six Throwers, five Healers and one Ice Golem, with Barbarian King and Troop Launcher. The latter also has six Invisibility Spells, Recall, Rage, Overgrowth, two Totems and Poison across its listed spell inventory. A Thrower substitution requires the corresponding troop inventory. The King variant requires replacing Duke in the hero roster; its ability order comes specifically from b46w2PUASJI.

u9owFe-ervU supplies the Super Archer variant, two scouting Balloons, two Ice Golems and a Stun Blaster Duke, but leaves Root Rider, Super Archer and Healer totals unstated. No Super Archer quantity is invented. Ff0NfWFgSiY instead names two Super Yetis and leaves its Root Rider total unstated.

Other substantial compositions include eQAelt6VLeE's four Root Riders, three Valkyries, five Healers, two Ice Golems and one Druid, and WlWHcFAz7ys's similar four-Root-Rider, three-Valkyrie army. Both carry five Invisibility Spells, Recall and two Overgrowth Spells. Their two-Overgrowth sequencing differs from the default, and no expiration duration is invented.

QBJSv33_sIc describes a continuous Royal Champion and Grand Warden walk without a narrated Recall. Its Town Hall variant above extracts the Overgrowth and saved-Spear policy. Overgrowth expiration and exact Town Hall arrival are not available triggers, and the source states no numeric wait. The required zero-delay fallback cannot enforce the narrated expiration timing or guarantee Rocket Spear targets the Town Hall.

The narration does not supply a complete executable deployment schedule for every carried utility troop or every spell. Unspecified default uses of Earthquakes, the remaining Totem, Rocket Balloons, Apprentice Warden, cleanup troops and the remaining Balloon are intentionally unscheduled. No repeat interval, cleanup percentage, automatic siege release or troop batch is invented.

Variants are alternative substitutions and are not automatically cumulative. Variants introducing different troops, heroes, equipment, spells or siege machines require their stated source composition; the default army does not supply those additional inventories. Reused step ids preserve dependency references and do not necessarily retain their original action meaning.
